title: Ladybugs Among the Leaves
description: Look closely at a ladybug through its beetle body, spotted wing covers, and tiny prey.
cardDescription: Look closely at a ladybug through its beetle body, spotted wing covers, and tiny prey.
focus: Ladybugs are beetles, and their hard forewings cover a separate flying pair. The clues distinguish the adult body from younger stages and from the insects it may eat.
solvingTip: Use the number or position of a body part. A covering, a feeler, and a food animal have different names.
words: American name for a small rounded beetle often marked with spots
One hardened beetle forewing covering the folded flying wings
Small plant-feeding insect eaten by many ladybugs
Immature feeding stage before a ladybug becomes a pupa
One paired feeler on a ladybug's head
Insect group characterized by hardened forewing covers
Small contrasting mark on many ladybug wing covers
Thin flight surface folded beneath a beetle's hard cover
Plant surface on which a ladybug may search for prey
One of an insect's six walking limbs
Body region carrying a ladybug's eyes and feelers
Early ladybug life stage often laid near a food supply
Stage between larva and adult in a ladybug's life cycle

answerNotes.LADYBUG: Ladybugs are beetles; not every species has the familiar red background with black spots.
answerNotes.ELYTRON: Elytron is singular, while elytra is plural; these hard covers are modified forewings.
answerNotes.APHID: Many ladybugs prey on aphids, though not every species has the same diet.
answerNotes.LARVA: A ladybug larva looks different from the rounded adult beetle.
answerNotes.ANTENNA: Antennae are sensory structures, separate from the six walking legs.

title: An Ant Colony Under the Path
description: Explore an ant colony through its members, underground chambers, and food-gathering activity.
cardDescription: Explore an ant colony through its members, underground chambers, and food-gathering activity.
subtheme: An Ant Colony Under the Path
focus: Ant colonies organize work among different individuals. The clues identify roles and structures without treating a colony’s queen as a human-style commander.
solvingTip: Separate the animal’s role from the space it occupies and the route it follows.
words: Social insect commonly living in an organized colony
Reproductive female in an ant colony
Usually nonreproductive female performing an ant colony's daily tasks
Community of ants living and functioning together
Passage connecting spaces in an underground ant nest
Enlarged roomlike space within an ant nest
Route followed by a line of food-gathering ants
Home structure occupied by an ant colony
Ground material excavated by many nesting ants
Legless young stage cared for by adult ants
Developing stage before an ant emerges as an adult
Material gathered to nourish the colony
Mouthpart used by an ant for gripping or carrying
Chemical signal helping many ants follow a route

answerNotes.ANT: Ants are insects with six legs; their colonies vary greatly in size and behavior.
answerNotes.QUEEN: A queen's primary role is reproduction, not issuing commands like a human monarch.
answerNotes.WORKER: Worker ants perform jobs such as foraging and brood care; the exact division varies among species.
answerNotes.COLONY: Colony names the social group rather than just its underground nest structure.
answerNotes.TUNNEL: A tunnel is a connecting route; a chamber is an enlarged space reached along it.

title: An Earthworm After a Spring Shower
description: Follow an earthworm through damp soil, garden roots, and the small openings it leaves.
cardDescription: Follow an earthworm through damp soil, garden roots, and the small openings it leaves.
subtheme: An Earthworm After a Spring Shower
focus: These clues use ordinary garden and weather words to describe the worm's surroundings and movement.
solvingTip: Start with a weather word or something found in the ground.
words: Long soft animal that moves through garden soil
Passage made through soil by a burrowing worm
Garden earth through which the worm moves
Move by twisting the body from side to side
Water from clouds that leaves the garden damp
Slightly wet, as soil is after a light shower
Make a hole in the ground with a tool or the hands
Fallen tree part lying above the worm's soil
Plant part growing through the garden earth
Not hard or rigid, as an earthworm's body is
Surface beneath a garden walker's feet
Narrow walkway beside the damp garden bed
Small opening leading into the ground
Earthy color of much garden soil

answerNotes.EARTHWORM: Earthworms are animals without legs, rather than insects.
answerNotes.TUNNEL: A tunnel is the passage, while a hole can be its opening.
answerNotes.SOIL: Soil contains mineral particles and organic material.
answerNotes.WRIGGLE: Wriggling describes the movement of the worm's flexible body.
answerNotes.RAIN: Rain wets the surface and changes the conditions in the garden.

title: Dew Drops on a Spider Web
description: Look at a spider's web through shining dew, fine threads, and the small creatures around it.
cardDescription: Look at a spider's web through shining dew, fine threads, and the small creatures around it.
subtheme: Dew Drops on a Spider Web
focus: The spider makes silk threads. Dew drops can make those threads easier to see in the morning.
solvingTip: The short words for drops and threads help with the animal's name.
words: Eight-legged animal that can make silk threads
Network of threads made by many spiders
Fine material a spider makes for its threads
Water drops forming on cool surfaces overnight
One fine strand in a spider's web
One small bead of water on the web
Small round shape made by a drop of dew
Small winged insect that a spider may catch
One of a spider's eight walking limbs
Make a silk thread, as a spider does
Be suspended between the web's supports
Trap a small insect in the web
Able to hold an insect that touches the web
Plant part beside the shining web

answerNotes.SPIDER: A spider has eight legs; insects have six.
answerNotes.WEB: Different spiders make different webs, and some do not use a web to catch prey.
answerNotes.SILK: Spider silk is made by the animal rather than gathered from a plant.
answerNotes.DEW: Dew is moisture that condenses on surfaces rather than falling as rain.
answerNotes.THREAD: Many connected threads make up the web's structure.

title: A Snail on the Garden Wall
description: Follow a snail through its shell, slow movement, and damp surroundings beside the garden.
cardDescription: Follow a snail through its shell, slow movement, and damp surroundings beside the garden.
subtheme: A Snail on the Garden Wall
focus: The snail carries its shell as it moves. A shiny trail may be visible behind it.
solvingTip: Start with a color-free texture or movement word.
words: Slow-moving animal often carrying a coiled shell
Hard covering carried by the garden snail
Slippery material that can form a snail's trail
Line left behind as the snail moves
Move slowly along a surface, as a snail does
Not fast, as the snail's pace is
Green plant part beside the crawling animal
Upright garden surface supporting the snail
Not hard, as the body beneath the shell is
Slightly wet, as a garden wall may be after rain
Water from clouds that wets the garden
Hard natural object near the snail's route
Planted area beside the old wall
Underground plant part near the damp soil

answerNotes.SNAIL: The shell protects much of the snail's soft body.
answerNotes.SHELL: A shell is part of the animal's body rather than a loose garden stone.
answerNotes.SLIME: A snail produces mucus that can leave a visible shiny trace.
answerNotes.TRAIL: A trail records the route rather than being part of the shell.
answerNotes.CRAWL: Crawling describes movement over the wall rather than through the air.
